concrete_examples.description: In NetHack, the stealth and awareness system is implemented through various mechanics such as line-of-sight and the ability of monsters to detect the player based on visibility and noise. Players can utilize stealth tactics, such as moving silently or hiding in shadows, to avoid detection and engage in strategic gameplay.

In broguece, the stealth and awareness system is implemented through a visibility mechanic where monsters have a line-of-sight that determines if they can detect the player based on distance and obstacles. Players can use stealth tactics like moving quietly and utilizing darkness to avoid detection and engage in strategic combat.

In 'crawl', the stealth and awareness system is implemented through mechanics such as line-of-sight, where enemies can only detect the player if they are within their field of vision, and through various environmental factors like darkness, which can obscure the player's presence, allowing for tactical approaches to combat and exploration.

In cataclysm-bn, the stealth and awareness system is implemented through a combination of line-of-sight mechanics and noise generation; players can move quietly to avoid detection by creatures, while environmental factors like light levels and terrain type affect visibility and awareness ranges. Players can utilize stealth tactics to navigate around threats without engaging in combat, enhancing tactical depth.

definition: A game mechanic where visibility and detection affect gameplay — creatures can be aware or unaware of the player, and stealth tactics can avoid or delay combat. Line-of-sight, lighting, and noise create tactical depth.
exclusion_criteria: Games where all creatures are always aware of the player
Pure combat games without stealth options
inclusion_criteria: Creatures have awareness states (asleep, awake, alerted)
Player can avoid detection through stealth
Stealth creates tactical options beyond direct combat
title: Stealth and Awareness System
